newsitem.title: USA: NY legislation proposes solar incentives.
newsitem.headline: NY legislation proposes solar incentives.

text.p: New York Governor George Pataki Friday proposed legislation to encourge New Yorkers to invest in solar energy systems for their homes by providing an ineome tax credit, his office said.
The proposal would also allow residential customers receive the full retail value of power generated by these systems, the governor's statement said.
It said the bill requires electric utilities to interconnect residential solar equipment ot their systems and provide "net metering" for residential customers.

Net metering is when the flow of electricity to and from a house is regulated through a single meater that measures the difference the power supplied by the solar system beyond the needs of the home and power purchased when the solar system was not providing the home's needs.
This allows homeowners to apply the excess power generated against their monthly bills, the statement pointed out.
To help make solar systems more affordable, the bill provides a personal income tax credit for individuals who invest in solar energy for residental use.
The credit would be 25 percent of the cost of the equipment, up to a maximum of $3,750.

The utilities operating in New York state include Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Central Hudson Gas and Electric Corp, New York State Electric and Gas Corp, Rochester Gas and Electric Corp, Long Island Lighting Co and Niagara Mohawk Power Corp.
